summary.headline: KIMS Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41.3% YoY to INR1,363 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 20.5% amid new-unit ramp-up drag.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR1,344 crore (up 39.9% YoY, 14% QoQ) and PAT was INR76 crore versus INR37 crore in Q1 FY27. Reported EBITDA was INR279 crore (margin 20.5%, versus 21.7% a year earlier), with ramp-up costs at Kondapur, Oncology launches in Andhra Pradesh and newer Bengaluru and Thane units weighing on margins. Management said Q2 is the bottom for margins and expects an upward trajectory, while acquisitions (Sarvottam/KIMS Trust Kakinada, O&M deals) and capacity additions continued. Net debt is guided at about INR2,150 crore (about 1.9x net debt/EBITDA).

financial_highlights.change: +34% YoY, +16.3% QoQ; margin vs 21.7% in Q2 FY26 and 20.1% in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA pre-Ind AS excluding other income

financial_highlights.change: vs INR72 crore in Q2 FY26 and INR37 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and equivalents incl. MF and short-term deposits

segments.name: Telangana cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from INR623 crore to INR700 crore QoQ, mainly from the new Kondapur hospital (500 of its beds commissioned, about 70-75% occupancy) and Secunderabad. Management said Kondapur revenue grew at least 70% after the move from the old facility; EBITDA margin dipped, targeted to return to about 30% over the next three to four quarters.

segments.name: Andhra Pradesh cluster
segments.commentary: Top-line growth strong, but margin compressed. Reported EBITDA about INR55 crore; adding back INR8 crore of doubtful-debt provision gives about INR63 crore, roughly 25% margin, per management. Two oncology programmes (Vizag, Anantapur) add about INR2 crore per month of fixed cost per centre; Vizag reportedly back to 28-29% margin by late October.

segments.name: Maharashtra cluster
segments.commentary: Occupancy above 60% with under 700 operating beds against more than 950 capacity; about 75 idle beds in Thane and about 150 in Nashik, to be operationalised as ramp-up happens. Nashik gained GIPSA empanelment, covering 40-50% of insurance volume.

segments.name: Bengaluru cluster (Mahadevapura, Electronic City, Thane-related)
segments.commentary: Mahadevapura has reached EBITDA breakeven; Electronic City broke even in September 2026, with management guiding quarterly breakeven in Q4 FY27. Only about 340 of 800 beds in Bengaluru are operational; management targets about 70% occupancy over four to six years from commissioning.

segments.name: Kakinada (KIMS Trust Hospital)
segments.commentary: Acquired 51% for INR80 crore (183 beds per the presentation, 150 beds per Q&A); currently about INR8-10 crore monthly revenue with EBITDA of INR1.2-1.5 crore per month and 38-40% occupancy. Target of INR12-15 crore monthly revenue in one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the potential revenue and margin impact of trade margin rationalisation on anti-cancer drugs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said final details were not yet disclosed (expected 9 November), so no quantification; oncology is not a big revenue share, so impact may not be significant.

qa_highlights.question: What are growth and margin ex the new Kondapur unit in Telangana?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana revenue rose from INR623 crore to INR700 crore QoQ, mostly from Kondapur and Secunderabad; EBITDA absolute number rose but percentage dipped, with margins expected back to about 30% over three to four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kondapur's break-even sustained, and what are occupancy levels?
qa_highlights.answer: No losses at Kondapur, but fixed costs are higher; about 500 beds commissioned at 70-75% occupancy, with the rest to be commissioned in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AP margins decline and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Adding back INR8 crore doubtful-debt provision, AP EBITDA is about INR63 crore (~25% margin) vs reported INR55 crore; the drag is two onco programmes at about INR2 crore/month per centre. Vizag back to 28-29% margin by late October; Anantapur needs at least a year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin trajectory from here and what is the exit run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is the bottom; trajectory should be upward unless new hospitals are commissioned in the coming months. Only one of 28 operational hospitals (Electronic City) is still EBITDA negative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Electronic City breakeven timing and insurance status for Thane and Mahadevapura?
qa_highlights.answer: Electronic City broke even in September 2026; quarterly breakeven guided to Q4 FY27. Thane lacks two or three major insurers; Mahadevapura lacks GIPSA, Star and others; full empanelment expected towards year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Secunderabad bed situation and plan to lift Telangana occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Secunderabad has 1,000 capacity with about 700 operational including ~80 dialysis machines as non-census beds; 250 beds under renovation to be made operational, with potential to reach 1,250 beds. Management expects Telangana occupancy at 55-60% of operational beds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of O&M to ownership conversion and call option multiples?
qa_highlights.answer: Call option to buy O&M assets at 10-12x trailing EBITDA, fixed at contract signing. Sarvottam/KIMS Trust Kakinada acquired 51% for INR80 crore; O&M call option gives 9% of top line, with fair value gain of INR13.2 crore booked below EBITDA in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex cash outflow, new debt rationale and Kakinada economics?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 capex about INR650 crore; about INR1,100 crore over next 18 months. Debt tied up for projects; QIP proceeds 25% earmarked for general corporate purposes and parked in MFs/bank. Kakinada: INR8-10 crore monthly revenue, EBITDA INR1.2-1.5 crore/month, 38-40% occupancy; 49% held by existing doctor, buy option at fixed multiples.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 described as the bottom for margins; management expects an upward trajectory from here absent new hospital commissioning in the next few months.
Kondapur margins expected to return to about 30% over the next three to four quarters; Kondapur remaining 500 beds to be commissioned within the next two quarters.
Electronic City (Bengaluru) expected to reach quarterly EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 (September 2026 was a monthly breakeven).

Andhra Pradesh: Vizag oncology back to 28-29% margin by late October; Anantapur oncology needs at least a year to reach healthy margins; AP margins expected to normalise over the next two to three quarters.

Kakinada (KIMS Trust) target of INR12-15 crore monthly revenue within one to two years, from INR8-10 crore currently; Bengaluru 800-bed hospitals targeted at ~70% occupancy over four to six years from commissioning.

Net debt about INR2,150 crore, net debt/EBITDA about 1.9x; minority share of EBITDA expected at 10-15% over the next several quarters; Kondapur old-facility fixed cost of INR1.5 crore/month for four to five more months. Net capex outflow of about INR1,100 crore over the next ~18 months on Secunderabad, Rajahmundry and Kondapur; no significant bed addition beyond 400-500 beds over next 24 months.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex spent about INR650 crore, of which roughly INR275-300 crore went into Kondapur.
Three projects pending (Secunderabad, Rajahmundry, and residual Kondapur capex) with total outflow of about INR1,100 crore over the next ~18 months.
Kondapur: 500 of the full hospital's beds commissioned at about 70-75% occupancy; remaining beds to be commissioned in the next two quarters.
Secunderabad: 1,000 capacity but about 700 operational (non-census dialysis beds, ~80 machines); 250 beds under renovation to be operationalised in first phase, with potential to reach 1,250 beds.
Rajahmundry and Ongole expansions to be commissioned in the next four to five months; Anantapur (Saveera) doubled from 250 to 500 beds, inaugurated 1 November 2026.
Maharashtra: under 700 operating beds vs more than 950 capacity; ~75 idle beds in Thane and ~150 in Nashik. Bengaluru: only ~340 of 800 beds operational.
Chennai 300-bed hospital expected from FY2029/2030; further expansion planned in existing states over the next four to five years.

Kondapur rental partner: rent about INR5.5 crore/month (INR60-65 crore annually incl. GST); management evaluating acquiring ~60% of the associate (KIMS holds ~40%) via merger, decision in about 12 months; would add about INR400 crore debt.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per operating bed up 14.9% YoY and 2.3% QoQ; average revenue per patient up 9.9% YoY and 1.2% QoQ.
IP volumes 81,668 (+27% YoY, +12.7% QoQ); OP volumes 731,010 (+23.3% YoY, +11% QoQ).
Telangana cluster revenue rose from INR623 crore to INR700 crore QoQ; Kondapur revenue up at least 70% after the move from the old facility over three months.

Andhra Pradesh: top-line growth strong but margin compressed; INR8 crore doubtful-debt provision (INR7.5-7.8 crore per CFO) on government scheme receivables, expected to reverse in Q3 or Q4 on collection. Two oncology programmes add about INR2 crore/month fixed cost per centre.
Insurance: Nashik got GIPSA empanelment (40-50% of insurance volume); Thane lacks two to three major insurers and Mahadevapura lacks GIPSA, Star and others; negotiations on pricing ongoing.
Oncology trade margin rationalisation on anti-cancer drugs: final details awaited around 9 November; management said oncology is not a large part of revenue, so impact may not be significant.
risks_watch: Margin recovery at Kondapur, Vizag/Anantapur oncology and Electronic City depends on ramp-up; management has set timelines of three to four quarters and Q4 FY27.
Doubtful-debt provisions on AP government receivables (INR8 crore in Q2) and reversal timing dependent on collections in Q3/Q4.
Insurance empanelment still incomplete at Thane, Mahadevapura and Electronic City; pricing negotiations ongoing with two or three insurers each.
Oncology trade margin rationalisation details pending (expected 9 November) with unquantified impact on revenue and margins.
Rising rental cost (Ind AS 116) from Kondapur; possible merger of rental entity adds about INR400 crore debt. Kerala government's proposed private hospital charge regulation has no visibility yet.
Minority buyouts and debt-funded capex; net debt about INR2,150 crore at 1.9x, with minority share of EBITDA expected at 10-15%.
key_quotes: This is the bottom Q2 number. I think from here, the trajectory should be upward.
Over the next three, four quarters, it should come back to a 30% kind of a margin.
We have a call option to buy these O&M assets anywhere in the range of 10 to 12 trailing EBITDA.
We are very, very confident that it can able to ramp up next one or two years, about INR7 crores-INR8 crores per month, can go up to INR12 crores-INR15 crores.
summary.management_tone: "Confident on medium-term ramp-up and margin recovery, with explicit timelines for Kondapur, AP oncology and Electronic City. Evasive or deferred on oncology pricing impact, minority buyouts and Kerala regulation, saying figures or plans are not yet firm."

growth.why: Management guides margin recovery (Kondapur back to ~30% in 3-4 quarters, Electronic City breakeven in Q4 FY27, Q2 called the margin bottom), backed by 500 Kondapur beds still to commission in two quarters, Secunderabad 250-bed renovation, and ramp-up in Maharashtra and Bengaluru idle beds; bed additions slow to 400-500 over 24 months.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 is called the margin bottom at 20.5% reported EBITDA margin (vs 21.7% a year ago); Kondapur targeted back to about 30% over 3-4 quarters, Vizag oncology to 28-29% by late October, and AP margins to normalise over 2-3 quarters, with the INR8 crore doubtful-debt provision expected to reverse in Q3 or Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kondapur's remaining 500 beds are due within two quarters, Rajahmundry and Ongole expansions within 4-5 months, and Anantapur (Saveera) doubled to 500 beds was inaugurated 1 November 2026; about 400-500 beds more over 24 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: IP volumes rose 27% YoY and OP volumes 23.3% YoY in Q2, with Kondapur at 70-75% occupancy on 500 beds, Secunderabad's 250-bed renovation to lift Telangana occupancy to 55-60%, and Maharashtra and Bengaluru idle beds (about 225 in Maharashtra, about 460 in Bengaluru) still to be filled.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 70-75% and about INR1,100 crore is already committed over 18 months across Secunderabad, Rajahmundry and Kondapur, so a new capex announcement is not signalled; a Kondapur associate merger (about INR400 crore of debt) is under evaluation with a decision in about 12 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is guiding to recovery rather than raising targets, and the net debt/EBITDA of about 1.9x and the oncology trade-margin rationalisation (details due around 9 November, unquantified) cap any near-term upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Electronic City breakeven was pushed from Q3 to Q4 FY27, Kondapur fixed costs of INR1.5 crore/month continue for 4-5 months, and insurance empanelment is still incomplete at Thane, Mahadevapura and Electronic City.

rows.label: Electronic City quarterly EBITDA breakeven
rows.why: Monthly breakeven reached in September 2026 and management guided quarterly breakeven to Q4 FY27 (cut from Q3), the only one of 28 operational hospitals still EBITDA negative.

rows.why: Nashik gained GIPSA empanelment covering 40-50% of insurance volume; Thane and Mahadevapura empanelment expected towards year-end, with pricing negotiations ongoing with two or three insurers each.
